correctness.rationale: TARGET route audited normally. Weak-duality inference is valid: any linear certificate proving Aw<=binomial on the polytope must have value >= primal max Pw, so Pw>binomial rules out real-LP Krawtchouk certificates at those points. Binomial values (0.410156, 0.480118, 2.59264), xi1 values (0.1601, 0.1835) and xi2 no-root gaps (>=0.23) were independently recomputed exactly and match. Krawtchouk rows verified integer-exact. n=15 optimum independently reproduced to ~5.6 by vertex sampling vs claimed 5.63636. n=31 residuals (minA>=-7e-05, sum residual<=7.2e-04) are negligible against 11-46x margins, and scope is honestly limited to real-LP with no integrality or code-existence claim.

originality.rationale: Fused 20-result search over literal, equivalent, and dominance formulations plus full-text inspection of the ABL source (doi:10.1109/18.915662, all 62635 chars) shows no prior finite-n primal maxima Pw at (15,7,4)/(31,15,7) for w=2,4,5 and no certificate-nonexistence computation there. ABL Corollaries 2-3 give asymptotic binomiality thresholds via sufficient feasible polynomials; failure of one polynomial family does not imply the computed LP optima, and no table or hierarchy paper lists these point values. The 3-point numerical barrier is substantively new.

value.rationale: The headline is three tiny-n point evaluations (n=15,31; w=2,4,5) showing the real-LP relaxation exceeds the binomial value below the xi1 branch. The admitted target asked for an asymptotic open set epsilon-extension ruling or Delsarte-MacWilliams LP-optimality of xi_ABL; the draft explicitly claims neither and retreats to finite-n localizations. Fixed small-weight LP slack where binomial<1 is a cheap small-instance mismatch and arbitrary finite slice under the shared standard: it does not resolve the asymptotic question, provides no general criterion, census, benchmark, or downstream use, and the precise numbers 5.63636/22.2762/29.4919 were not motivated before computation as a recognized needed fact. Correctness plus novelty do not create value.

checked_sources: ABL original paper doi:10.1109/18.915662 full text (62635 chars, offsets 0-62635): asymptotic feasible-polynomial bounds, Corollaries 2-3 xi thresholds, no finite-n Pw table

scope_literature_search EMERGENT_ORIGINALITY 3-direction fused set (20 results, full provider coverage, no partial failure): ABL source, Delsarte LP hierarchy, MRRW, Sage bounds, constant-weight tables
Independent recomputation: exact binomials via comb, xi1 formula, xi2 entropy gap scan reproducing min gaps 0.23349/0.23332, integer Krawtchouk rows for w=2,4,5
Independent LP cross-check: numpy vertex enumeration reproducing n=15 Aw~5.6 (ratio ~13.65) and artifact residual review (lp_verify.txt, lp_primal.csv)

broader_coverage.evidence: Hierarchy and MRRW papers prove general strength/rate relations; ABL proves sufficient-condition binomiality intervals. None computes finite-n Aw primal maxima at (15,7,4)/(31,15,7) or rules on real-LP certificates there.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader asymptotic or hierarchy theorem does not cover the claim as a special case because the claim is a point-wise numerical LP lower bound, not a corollary of those upper-bound or structural theorems.
broader_coverage.search: Searched Delsarte LP hierarchy, MRRW rate bounds, Samorodnitsky LP optimum, and ABL asymptotic binomiality range for a stronger theorem subsuming the three points

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: ABL feasibility is sufficient-only so its failure implies nothing about all LP certificates; binomial<1 alone does not fix LP maxima at 5.63, 22.28, 29.49, which required solving the constrained Krawtchouk LPs.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The point-wise barrier is not mechanically implied by prior work, so originality holds; however the computation remains an isolated tiny-n slice that does not imply the target asymptotic optimality question, hence value fails.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: Tested whether ABL polynomial failure, binomial value below 1 at tiny weights, or LP weakness mechanically implies the reported Pw magnitudes and nonexistence conclusion

equivalent_formulations.evidence: ABL uses distance distribution for the same object and Krawtchouk/dual-distance terminology, but its results are asymptotic upper-bound polynomials with no finite-n Pw values 5.63636, 22.2762, 29.4919 at the claimed parameters.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Synonymous notation does not create coverage: no equivalent-formulation source states or implies the specific primal-maxima numbers or the point-wise certificate-nonexistence conclusion.
equivalent_formulations.search: Searched distance distribution vs weight distribution vs binomial moments vs Krawtchouk coefficient synonymous encodings in fused queries and ABL full text

exact_database_or_table.evidence: Sage implements generic Delsarte size bounds via Krawtchouk matrices; code tables list [31,16,7] existence and best-known distances, not Aw primal maxima; no table lists the three Pw/binomial/ratio rows.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The exact numbers are not a direct lookup or database recomputation; table existence of the BCH codes only certifies polytope nonemptiness, not the computed optima.
exact_database_or_table.search: Searched Sage Delsarte bounds docs, best-binary-code tables, BCH weight tables, and constant-weight bound tables for the exact Pw entries

residual_risks: CBC LP optima lack exact rational dual certificates and pulp was unavailable for bit-exact re-solve; overturn unlikely given 11-46x margins, exact binomial/xi2 recomputation, and independent n=15 vertex reproduction.

source_inspections.inspection_evidence: Full-text read of theorem scope: ABL proves asymptotic upper bounds via sufficient feasible polynomials (Thms 6-7,12-13, Cors 2-3); contains no finite-n primal LP maxima at (15,7,4)/(31,15,7) and no real-LP certificate-nonexistence claim at w=2,4,5.
